constraints: Filters remain shareable through the URL; layout must not create another filter-state store.

feedback.reason: Use the component’s allocated space as its responsive boundary.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Container queries let a reusable component respond to its allocated space.
details.scenarioApplication: The filter’s containing block, exposed as an inline-size query container. Filters remain shareable through the URL; layout must not create another filter-state store.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The parent must establish a suitable size container; intrinsic wrapping still handles widths between explicit arrangements.
details.errorCorrection: Both placements share the viewport, so this cannot distinguish their allocated widths.
details.transfer: Use the same rule when the filter moves into a drawer.

messages.text: Both placements share the viewport, so this cannot distinguish their allocated widths.
Label size affects wrapping but does not measure the space allocated by the parent.

Choose the arrangement from the longest filter label.

prompt: A store manager opens the same inventory filter in a 320px sidebar and a 700px workspace within one browser window. Each placement needs its own stacked or inline arrangement. Which size should drive that choice?

constraints: The layout change must preserve the current card task and logical reading order.

feedback.reason: Reflow should preserve the active card task.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Responsive presentation can change without replacing interactive nodes.
details.scenarioApplication: Keep card identity and DOM order; change the column layout with CSS. The layout change must preserve the current card task and logical reading order.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Remote conflict resolution remains a data concern; CSS must not silently reinterpret a move.
details.errorCorrection: Promoting the active column visually can separate reading and keyboard order from the logical task order.
details.transfer: Verify focus continuity when a sidebar opens as well as when the viewport narrows.

messages.text: Promoting the active column visually can separate reading and keyboard order from the logical task order.
Restoring to a heading abandons the focused card action and remounting discards its identity.
A layout change is not a reason to suspend the shared-board contract; updates and focus must coexist.

options.text: Keep card identity and DOM order; change the column layout with CSS.
Keep DOM identity; use CSS order to promote the active column.
Remount cards in narrow-layout order and restore focus to the column heading.
Keep DOM order and disable remote updates until the layout is wide again.

prompt: A planning board changes from columns to stacked sections while a facilitator has keyboard focus on a card action. Remote updates are also arriving. How should the width change affect the mounted cards?

constraints: Document geometry is necessary for review; ordinary upload and review controls do not require a two-dimensional layout.

feedback.reason: Keep the spatial exception local to the document.

details.mechanismOrProperty: WCAG reflow permits localized two-dimensional content exceptions.
details.scenarioApplication: Keep the scanned document’s geometry inside its own viewer while headings, file controls and review actions reflow at 320 CSS pixels.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The exception does not extend to headings, review actions or other surrounding content.
details.errorCorrection: The document’s spatial need does not justify horizontal scrolling for ordinary review controls.
details.transfer: Apply the same boundary to a map or a genuinely two-dimensional data table.

messages.text: The document’s spatial need does not justify horizontal scrolling for ordinary review controls.
Scaling shrinks text and controls instead of making ordinary content reflow.
Breaking the spatial document into reflowed tiles destroys the arrangement the task explicitly requires.

options.text: Convert the scanned document into independently wrapping visual tiles.
Scroll the document viewer; reflow the review controls.
Make the complete portal horizontally scrollable.
Scale the portal to fit, retaining the original fixed widths.

prompt: A case portal displays a scanned legal document whose two-dimensional spatial arrangement matters. At 320 CSS pixels, surrounding upload and review controls must remain usable. Where should horizontal scrolling be allowed?

constraints: The message direction is set on its content region; controls retain logical reading order.

feedback.reason: Direction and text expansion need compatible layout rules.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Logical properties follow writing direction; intrinsic layout accommodates text expansion.
details.scenarioApplication: Use logical inline spacing and allow labels and control groups to wrap. The message direction is set on its content region; controls retain logical reading order.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Direction metadata and plural selection still need their own semantic implementation.
details.errorCorrection: Logical spacing handles direction, but a fixed height can still clip expanded toolbar content.
details.transfer: Retest a long LTR translation too: expansion is not exclusive to RTL.

messages.text: Logical spacing handles direction, but a fixed height can still clip expanded toolbar content.

options.text: Swap physical margins and retain fixed label widths.
Use logical spacing; ellipsize every label to its original width.
Use logical spacing with wrapping labels and controls.
Use logical margins and a fixed-height toolbar.

prompt: A translator switches an editor to Arabic and enters a long message. The editor is inside a narrow drawer. Which spacing and sizing rule survives both direction and text expansion?

constraints: Use CSS-pixel viewport dimensions rather than the physical pixel count of the device.

feedback.reason: Test the CSS width required by the reflow criterion.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Reflow is evaluated at an equivalent width of 320 CSS pixels for vertically scrolling content.
details.scenarioApplication: Check the form at 320 CSS pixels wide without page-level horizontal scrolling. Use CSS-pixel viewport dimensions rather than the physical pixel count of the device.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Vertical scrolling is allowed; this does not require every field on one screen.
details.errorCorrection: Text resizing is a separate criterion; it does not establish reflow at the required width.
details.transfer: Desktop zoom can create the equivalent narrow CSS viewport when the test is configured correctly.

messages.text: Text resizing is a separate criterion; it does not establish reflow at the required width.
Device pixels do not establish the CSS viewport width used by the reflow criterion.
Being above the fold does not establish reflow; vertical scrolling is allowed.

options.text: Check 200% text resizing at desktop width.
Check at a 320-device-pixel display resolution.
Check whether every field fits above the fold at 100% zoom.
Test at 320 CSS pixels without horizontal page scrolling.

prompt: A permitting form must meet WCAG 2.2 AA reflow. Its ordinary fields and submit action contain no content that requires a two-dimensional layout. Which acceptance test targets reflow?

constraints: The active player, playback position and caption state must survive a width change.

feedback.reason: Resize the player without replacing its stateful instance.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Responsive sizing should preserve the stateful media instance.
details.scenarioApplication: Keep one player mounted and size its wrapper responsively with an aspect ratio. The active player, playback position and caption state must survive a width change.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Controls and captions also need space; an aspect ratio alone does not prove their usability.
details.errorCorrection: Time alone does not restore captions, buffered playback or all other player state.

messages.text: Time alone does not restore captions, buffered playback or all other player state.

options.text: Resize the existing player within an aspect-ratio wrapper.

prompt: A learner resizes a course page while a video is playing with captions enabled. The video should fit the content column without restarting playback. Which implementation fits?

constraints: Preview width changes presentation; they do not grant publication permission.

feedback.reason: An embedded preview needs its own responsive boundary.

details.mechanismOrProperty: An embedded component can query its containing size independently of the outer viewport.
details.scenarioApplication: A size container around the preview’s responsive components. Preview width changes presentation; they do not grant publication permission.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A full-page viewport simulation may instead need a dedicated browsing context; a container is not a substitute for every viewport feature.
details.errorCorrection: The outer desktop viewport stays wide while the preview panel narrows.

messages.text: The outer desktop viewport stays wide while the preview panel narrows.
A desktop author can deliberately test a narrow component without changing device type.

options.text: Scale a fixed-width preview canvas to fit the panel.

Query the outer viewport from each preview block.
Select preview styles from the author’s device type.

prompt: An authoring suite embeds a lesson preview in a resizable panel on a wide desktop. The preview must show how its own blocks behave in a narrow placement. Which responsive boundary is useful?

constraints: The reading position and focused notification action should remain stable.

feedback.reason: Preserve the reader’s place through layout changes.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Handling arrival announcements and server read-state remains separate from responsive layout.

messages.text: Keeping nodes is useful, but resetting the reading anchor still interrupts the current task.

options.text: Switch focus between separate wide and narrow lists.
Preserve the scroll offset numerically while replacing every row node.
Reflow existing keyed rows and preserve the current reading anchor.
Reflow keyed rows and reset the list to its newest item.

prompt: A customer is reading a notification in a message list. New items arrive, and opening a side panel narrows the list. How should the list adapt?

constraints: A card’s layout must work independently of where the shell places it.

feedback.reason: Match each query to the scope of its layout decision.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Intrinsic card wrapping may remove the need for an explicit query at some sizes.
details.errorCorrection: The narrow rail can require a compact card even when the viewport and shell remain wide.

messages.text: The narrow rail can require a compact card even when the viewport and shell remain wide.
An individual card’s allocation does not describe the global navigation’s available space.
One flag collapses distinct shell and card boundaries that can need different modes simultaneously.

options.text: Use viewport breakpoints for both shell and cards.
Use each card container to choose the shell’s mode.
Use one global compact flag for all responsive regions.
Use viewport queries for the shell and container queries for card arrangements.

options.text: A chronological agenda sharing event selection.
Compress the week grid and abbreviate event titles.
Use an agenda with independent selected-event state.

prompt: A shared calendar shows a week grid on wide screens. On a narrow screen, all event titles and actions must remain readable, and an agenda view is permitted. Which narrow layout fits?

constraints: Approval remains server-authorized; responsive changes must preserve the review sequence.

feedback.reason: Keep review evidence connected to its decision actions.

options.text: Retain the review row and shrink its text to fit.

constraints: Older query responses must not overwrite newer results; layout changes do not alter that rule.

options.text: Hide the least-visible comparison columns at narrow widths.

constraints: The map enhances the result task; it is not the only way to select a place.
